result.note: Tests the India–Chile CEPA timeline and scope, and Chile's critical mineral profile; Goyal's conditional remarks on finalisation are skipped as speculative.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the proposed India–Chile Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), as of May 2026:
items: It would replace a Preferential Trade Agreement signed in 2006 and expanded in 2017.
Its negotiations were formally launched in April 2024 during Chilean President Gabriel Boric's visit to India.
It would cover digital services, MSMEs and critical minerals.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Negotiations were launched during Boric's visit in April 2025, and April 2024 is when the Joint Study Group report was finalised. TBB's analysis notes the CEPA is less a trade deal than a play for access to minerals.
questions.source: Negotiations were formally launched during Chilean President Gabriel Boric's visit to India in April 2025, following a Joint Study Group report finalised in April 2024.

questions.prompt: In May 2026, Chile's Foreign Minister visited New Delhi to advance a trade agreement with India. Chile holds the world's largest reserves of which mineral?
questions.explain: Chile holds the world's largest lithium reserves and is also the leading global copper producer. Both are key inputs for batteries, electric vehicles and clean energy infrastructure.
questions.source: Chile holds the world's largest lithium reserves and is the leading global copper producer.
